I read the comics and the author made a good job of explaining his opinions. My points are:

  1. I do not agree that standard of living of an American is more important than any other person. A lot of jobs in US may be lost, but they will be gained elsewhere. Why should I care more for prospects of a stranger in Oklahoma than a stranger in Jakarta?
  2. I believe countries should compete in attraction of capital. Both philosophical reason (physical and legal entities should be free to move capital anywhere in the universe if they wish to) and that competition between countries will make better entrepreneurial climate. Each country would strife to have legal security, ease of setting up business, low taxation, strong infrastructure... There is a bit of that competition now but the more open world, the stronger that pressure is. The stronger pressure equals better results.
  3. The panel where fat investors are threatening to move jobs somewhere else is presented as negative, but is very much needed. The labor laws need big overhaul, they are more fit for world of 1930's than today. Current protest of Paris taxi drivers against Uber show it very well.
  4. Author made some cheap shots at emotions. Every rich person is fat, smoking cigar and taking other's money by essentially fraud. I really don't think it reflects reality very well and the nameless poor masses are often exhibiting less moral principles than elites.
  5. Author makes a claim that standard of living is lower than in 1970's in the US. It is often repeated claim, but the studies are controversial at best. I think the standard of living of the same people is undeniably growing and you see that statistic because of (initially) poor immigrants and poor people having more kids. If you tag an average person in 1970's and their children, it will show they are better off.
  6. Everything bad in the comics is blamed on the freedom of capital movement and lack of regulation. Essentially everything could be presented in reverse by somebody with another opinion: the factories are closed because of the increased regulation since the 70's and every advantage is due to free trade. This comics makes me chuckle.
  7. It is true that China skews competition by devaluating Yuan. But it is not expenseless on their part. Devaluating currency is like borrowing from the future.
  8. I agree with the author on the subject of patents and copyright laws. Such laws should be similar and enforced. A clause about arbitrage in case of breaking them should have been a part of TPP.
  9. For international relations to work in any way international treaties must superseded local laws. Author criticizes that it hands over sovereignty to the Chinese, but it obviously cannot be the unbiased view. No trust and no cooperation would work without some power of international law on the legal one. Imagine you take your savings and invest them to the company in Brazil since they seem promising and have cool products. After that, Sao Paulo says: "Firms incorporated in Sao Paolo can keep their capital and not return any profits because we say so." You just lost your savings! But Brazil is sovereign so good for them.

The previous example obviously should not happen, and thus the precedence of international treaties is one of the base foundations of modern world. Problem is when it is not kept (military coup, new government, lack of power from central government, country goes bankrupt etc.). US Navy will not occupy Sao Paolo to return your investment (unless you are United Fruit in 1890's). It was by far the dumbest point author has made in the comics.

I absolutely believe that NAFTA, WTO, ASEAN and EU made the world a better place and similar international cooperation should continue.
